title: K-th Largest Perfect Subtree Size in Binary Tree
summary: Given a binary tree and an integer k, find the size of the k-th largest perfect binary subtree.
statement: Given a binary tree and an integer k, find the size of the k-th largest perfect binary subtree. If no such subtree exists, return -1. A perfect binary tree has all leaves at the same level and every parent node with two children.
constraints: The binary tree has 1–2,000 nodes and k is positive.
A perfect subtree has two perfect child subtrees of equal size; an empty child has size zero.
Return the kth-largest perfect-subtree size counting each root, or -1 if fewer than k exist.

reference_solution:
def kth_largest_perfect_subtree(root,k):
    sizes=[];computed={};stack=[(root,False)]
    while stack:
        node,visited=stack.pop()
        if node is None:continue
        if not visited:stack.extend(((node,True),(node.right,False),(node.left,False)));continue
        left=computed.get(id(node.left),0);right=computed.get(id(node.right),0)
        if left<0 or left!=right:computed[id(node)]=-1
        else:
            computed[id(node)]=left+right+1;sizes.append(computed[id(node)])
    sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    return sizes[k-1] if k<=len(sizes) else -1
